why: DNSSEC Steward is one end-to-end workflow, not a set of independent modules. It ships only when the whole workflow is proven from a clean install, under regression testing.

gates.title: Failover drill
gates.pass: Forced promotion and rejoin pass, with the time to signing measured
gates.evidence: Signing at the other site in 6 min 40 s; ns1 and ns3 rejoined

gates.title: Failback
gates.pass: Signing returns home through the normal, receipt-based handoff

gates.title: Open items closed
gates.pass: Build queue uniqueness rule aligned; the two readiness copies reconciled

gates.title: Steward installer
gates.pass: A Steward builds from the image on a clean node, on either CPU architecture

gates.title: Site data separated from code
gates.pass: Addresses, credentials and registrar settings are configuration; nothing of this cluster is in the repository

gates.title: Clean-room install
gates.pass: A fresh lab cluster, built only from the repository, signs a test zone end to end

gates.title: Full regression on the lab
gates.pass: Build, join, swap, unpublish, rollover, handoff, failover, rejoin and failback all pass in one run

gates.title: Documentation
gates.pass: Install, operate, recover, and the architecture

gates.title: Security and licence review
gates.pass: No secrets in the history, dependencies pinned, licence chosen
